tasks.description: Contact vetted Panama City legal contact to conduct registry search for 5 shell companies. Requires wire transfer for agent fee ($800). Can run in parallel with other registry checks.

tasks.title: Cross-reference leaked documents with verified registry data
tasks.description: Once registry verifications complete, systematically cross-check 2,400 pages of leaked Panama documents against verified corporate records. Identify discrepancies, confirm beneficial ownership chains. Can run partially in parallel with ongoing verifications.

tasks.description: Source A available Feb 12-13 only. Must schedule during Cyprus business hours (08:00-15:00 EET / 06:00-13:00 GMT) to allow real-time registry verification if needed. DEPENDENCY: Should complete Cyprus registry check first. Secure video call, record with consent, arrange transcription.

tasks.title: Interview Source B (beneficial ownership expert) - CRITICAL SEQUENCING
tasks.description: Source B available evenings Feb 14-16. **HOLDS MISSING LINK ON BENEFICIAL OWNERSHIP CHAIN** - this interview MUST happen BEFORE narrative draft, not after as initially planned. DEPENDENCY: Needs completed registry verifications and Source A interview context. Evening availability (after 19:00 GMT).

tasks.title: Draft narrative article - OPERATION CLEARVIEW
tasks.description: Write full investigative narrative (target: 3,500-4,000 words). DEPENDENCIES: Must have both interview transcripts, all registry verifications complete, documents cross-referenced. SEQUENCING CONFLICT RESOLVED: Move this AFTER Source B interview, not before.

tasks.title: Legal review by Morning Ledger counsel
tasks.description: Submit complete draft to legal team for defamation risk assessment, source protection review, jurisdiction-specific legal exposure analysis. HARD DEPENDENCY: Cannot start until draft complete AND all facts verified. If legal flags issues, halt publication workflow immediately (fail-fast).

tasks.title: Encrypted handoff to Editor Marcus Chen
tasks.description: Final legally-cleared draft transfer via encrypted channel. REQUIRES: Both Priya and Marcus online simultaneously. Marcus available Feb 18-19, 19:00-22:00 GMT. Use Signal + PGP-encrypted backup. DEPENDENCY: Legal review must be complete and cleared.

tasks.title: Expense report - CLEARVIEW investigation costs
tasks.description: Compile and submit expense report: Cyprus registry expedited search (£450), Panama agent fee ($800), secure transcription service, travel costs if any. Finance deadline end of month.

tasks.title: URGENT: Secure Signal call with Source A (Dmitri) - Dubai connection intel
tasks.description: Source A (Dmitri Kozlov) sent encrypted ProtonMail 2026-01-14 03:42 UTC with critical new intelligence: Apex Consolidated SA Dubai entity confirmed as third node in shell network. €4.2M wire transfers Dec 2025. Three-way flow: Cyprus->Malta->Dubai->Cyprus. Source window closing - being transferred internally next week. Must coordinate secure Signal call Thu/Fri (Jan 16-17) Cyprus evening time (UTC+2). Use established Signal drop protocol. Extract: wire transfer documentation, Apex SA registration details, beneficial owner signature patterns, timeline of fund movements. CRITICAL for CLEARVIEW article narrative.

tasks.title: Monitor Source B (Elena) communication blackout - assess compromise risk
tasks.description: Source B (Elena Volkov) reported 2026-01-14 that her audit firm is questioning document access patterns. Requested 72-hour communication blackout for safety assessment. DEADLINE: Monitor for contact by Monday 2026-01-19 EOD. If no contact received, assume source has been flagged/compromised and cannot proceed safely. Contingency: Elena stated existing documents (beneficial ownership chain Meridian->Sentinel) are sufficient for publication if cross-referenced with Cyprus registry. Prepare to proceed without additional Elena intel if necessary. Flag to Marcus and Legal (Rajesh) if source burned.

tasks.title: Verify Apex Consolidated SA Dubai - registry and beneficial ownership
tasks.description: New entity identified by Source A: Apex Consolidated SA, Dubai (DMCC registration suspected). Registered 2024. Alleged beneficial owner signature pattern matches Sentinel Cyprus and Meridian Malta. Verify: DMCC registry search for Apex Consolidated SA, registration date and beneficial owner records, corporate structure and nominee directors, connection to Cyprus/Malta entities. €4.2M wire transfer Dec 2025 requires documentary evidence. Coordinate with Dubai registry agent if needed. This is the "missing link" for three-jurisdiction shell network narrative.

tasks.title: Triage new UK shell network tip - assess credibility and scope
tasks.description: Received unsolicited encrypted tip 2026-01-15 from anonymous.tipster.2026@tutanota.com. Claims: UK-based shell network (12+ entities, London/Jersey/Cayman), £47M flow over 18 months, construction procurement fraud, source is UK bank compliance officer with internal memos and recordings. NOT related to CLEARVIEW but potentially larger scale. ASSESS: Source credibility (new/unverified contact), timeline feasibility (internal audit starting Feb 1st - pressure tactic?), resource allocation (CLEARVIEW deadline takes priority), honeypot/phishing risk. Consult Marcus before responding. May be legitimate new investigation thread for post-CLEARVIEW.

tasks.title: CHECKPOINT DECISION: Singapore source confirmation status (go/no-go)
tasks.description:
CRITICAL PATH DECISION POINT: Assess whether Source A (Dmitri K.) has provided Singapore beneficial ownership documents by Jan 6. If NO confirmation by checkpoint:
- Trigger contingency plan: scale back to Option B (BVI/Kenya only, redact Singapore entities)
- Cancel Kenya flight booking to avoid sunk cost
- Notify legal counsel of reduced scope
- Inform partner newsrooms of modified story angle

If YES confirmation received:
- Proceed with Option A (full three-jurisdiction story)
- Book Kenya flights immediately
- Fast-track legal clearance with Rajesh

Checkpoint meeting: Jan 6, 2pm with Marcus and Rajesh

- Wire transfer documentation he can provide
- Timeline of compliance violations
- Management response to his flagging
- Corroborating witnesses
- Security/anonymity concerns

- Backup publication angles

tasks.description: Panama corporate registry search for shell entities connecting Sentinel Holdings to ultimate beneficial owners. Formal request should have been submitted 5 days ago. No confirmation received from agent. Critical for completing shell network chain documentation. Rajesh (legal) flagging this as potential gap that could weaken allegations. Need immediate status update and expected delivery timeline. If documents won't arrive by Feb 26, must develop backup strategy for legal review.

tasks.title: Assess Singapore source (Tan Wei Ling) status - proceed without or delay?
tasks.description: Source Tan Wei Ling (Apex Maritime compliance officer) has been dark for 72+ hours. Last contact Feb 19. She provided initial beneficial ownership documents but additional verification was expected. This creates uncertainty for Singapore investigation branch. DECISION REQUIRED: (A) Proceed with existing documents and accept verification gap, or (B) Delay Singapore thread pending source re-contact. Impacts: Legal review timeline, partner newsroom coordination, publication scope. Discuss with Marcus at 2pm sync today.

tasks.title: Prepare interview question matrix - Source A & B cross-verification points
tasks.description: Develop detailed question matrix for Source A (Dimitri K., Cyprus interview Feb 25) and Source B (Elena V., beneficial ownership interview Feb 26). Focus on cross-verification points between sources to strengthen narrative. Key areas: (1) Beneficial ownership structure of Sentinel Holdings, (2) Timeline of fund transfers through Malta entities, (3) Dubai connection verification, (4) Document authentication. Must identify contradictions in advance and prepare follow-up questions. Critical for maximizing interview value given tight timeline to legal review.

tasks.description: Compile all investigation expenses for Q1 reporting: registry search fees (Cyprus, Jersey, Panama), encrypted communication services, source travel reimbursements, document translation costs. response_body.title: CLEARVIEW Registry Vendor Decision Analysis - GRD Flash Sale vs ECI Sunk Cost (April 2-4)
response_body.content:
DECISION CONTEXT (April 2, 2026 - 48hr window)

TRIGGER EVENT: GRD promotional email received 09:15 UTC
- Panama premium queries: €18/query (normally €25) 
- 24-hour turnaround guarantee
- 87% beneficial ownership success rate (vs ECI's 73%)
- Offer expires: April 4, 09:00 UTC
- "Limited journalist slots" urgency language

CURRENT STATE - ECI PACKAGE:
✓ Purchased: March 15, €450 total
✓ Consumed: 127 queries (€285 value used)
✗ Remaining: 73 queries (€285 unrecovered value)
✓ Expiration: April 30, 2026
✓ Coverage: Cyprus/Malta/Jersey
✗ Success rate: 73% (below 85% dual-source waiver threshold)
✗ Turnaround: 5-7 days standard processing

REMAINING CLEARVIEW ENTITIES: 27 total
Jurisdiction breakdown from investigation notes:
- Panama: 14 entities (critical path - shell network core)
- Cayman: 8 entities (critical path - beneficial ownership chain)
- Cyprus: 3 entities (non-critical - secondary verification)
- Jersey: 2 entities (non-critical - historical context)

LEGAL CONSTRAINT UPDATE (Rajesh Mehta, April 1):
✓ Dual-source waiver approved IF primary source ≥85% success rate
✓ GRD's 87% rate qualifies for waiver
✗ ECI's 73% rate requires dual-source verification
→ Legal review timeline impact: 4-6 days saved with waiver-qualified vendor

TIMELINE PRESSURE (Sarah Winters/Reuters, March 31):
✗ Publication deadline: April 10 (hard constraint - competitive pressure)
✗ Legal review deadline: April 7 (allows final edits)
✗ Documentation deadline: April 5 (legal review input)
→ Current date: April 2
→ Available buffer: 3 days for 27 entity queries + legal review

DECISION SCENARIOS:

SCENARIO A: Full GRD Switch (abandon ECI)
Cost calculation:
- GRD flash sale: 22 entities × €18 = €396
- ECI sunk cost loss: €285 (73 unused queries)
- Net cost: €681 total
- Additional spend: €396

Timeline impact:
- 24-hour GRD turnaround → documentation ready April 3
- Legal review April 3-6 (3 days, within buffer)
- Meets April 7 deadline with 1-day margin

Quality impact:
- 87% success rate → dual-source waiver approved
- Eliminates 4-6 day secondary verification step
- Certified translations included (saves legal review time)

Risks:
- €285 sunk cost unrecovered (budget efficiency hit)
- Vendor relationship damage with ECI (mid-contract abandonment)
- GRD urgency language may be manipulative (need verification)

SCENARIO B: Hybrid Approach
Cost calculation:
- Use ECI for 5 non-critical entities (Cyprus/Jersey): €0 additional
- GRD for 22 critical entities (Panama/Cayman): 22 × €18 = €396
- ECI sunk cost recovery: ~€15 (5 queries used from remaining 73)
- Net cost: €846 total
- Additional spend: €396

Timeline impact:
- ECI queries: 5-7 days → documentation ready April 7-9
- GRD queries: 24 hours → documentation ready April 3
- Legal review split: critical path April 3-6, non-critical April 7-9
- Meets April 7 deadline for critical entities only
- Non-critical entities miss publication window

Quality impact:
- Critical entities: 87% success rate, dual-source waiver
- Non-critical entities: 73% success rate, requires dual-source
- Mixed legal review complexity

Risks:
- Partial sunk cost recovery (€270 still unrecovered)
- Non-critical entities may miss publication deadline
- Increased coordination complexity (two vendors)

SCENARIO C: ECI-Only Continuation
Cost calculation:
- Use remaining 73 ECI queries: €0 additional
- Net cost: €450 total (already paid)
- Additional spend: €0
- Maximum sunk cost recovery

Timeline impact:
- 5-7 day turnaround → documentation ready April 7-9
- Legal review April 7-13 (includes dual-source verification)
- MISSES April 7 deadline by 6 days
- Publication deadline April 10 not feasible

Quality impact:
- 73% success rate → requires dual-source verification
- Adds 4-6 days to legal review timeline
- Higher defamation risk (below 85% threshold)

Risks:
- Publication deadline failure (competitive disadvantage)
- Partner newsroom coordination breakdown
- Legal review quality concerns (73% success rate)

VENDOR CREDIBILITY CHECK (GRD):
Need to verify:
□ Gmail history: prior GRD promotional emails (pattern analysis)
□ Finance records: past GRD transactions (relationship history)
□ "Limited journalist slots" claim: genuine capacity constraint or artificial urgency?
□ 87% success rate: independently verified or vendor claim?
□ References: Reuters/ICIJ/Guardian mentioned in email - verify?

DECISION CRITERIA WEIGHTING:
1. Timeline compliance (April 10 deadline): CRITICAL
2. Legal review quality (85%+ threshold): HIGH
3. Budget efficiency (sunk cost recovery): MEDIUM
4. Vendor relationship integrity: LOW

NEXT ACTIONS:
□ Search gmail for prior GRD emails (urgency pattern verification)
□ Check finance records for GRD transaction history
□ Cross-reference entity jurisdiction breakdown with investigation notes
□ Calculate legal review timeline buffer under each scenario
□ Draft decision memo documenting tradeoff analysis
□ If choosing A/B: prepare GRD order email with entity list
□ If choosing C: document rationale for future procurement protocol

DECISION DEADLINE: April 4, 09:00 UTC (48 hours from email receipt)

response_body.content:
INBOX TRIAGE ANALYSIS - APRIL 3, 2026

CRITICAL TIMELINE PRESSURE POINTS:

1. SOURCE A INTERVIEW WINDOW (HIGHEST PRIORITY)
- Final availability: April 7-9 only
- Must confirm by EOD April 3
- Documents time-sensitive (audit cycle closes April 15)
- Action: Reply to secure.contact.a@protonmail.com IMMEDIATELY to confirm April 7 slot
- Risk: Miss this window = lose critical Cyprus compliance documentation

2. LEGAL REVIEW DEADLINE - SINGAPORE ENTITIES (CRITICAL)
- Rajesh needs materials by EOD April 8
- Without these: Singapore thread cut OR 2-3 week publication delay
- Current blockers: (a) Still waiting on Meridian Asia registry docs, (b) Need to finalize source attribution framework
- Action: Prioritize Singapore documentation assembly April 4-7
- Risk: Legal insurance requirement = hard deadline, no flexibility

3. PARTNER COORDINATION DECISION (HIGH PRIORITY)
- Reuters/AIR need April 18 commitment by April 7
- Call scheduled April 4 15:00 GMT with Sarah
- Decision depends on: Singapore verification timeline + Source A interview completion
- Action: Prepare realistic timeline assessment for April 4 call
- Risk: Lose coordinated release advantage if we can't commit

4. PANAMA REGISTRY ACCESS (MEDIUM PRIORITY)
- Apex Consolidated SA = restricted access (7-10 days + €85)
- Alternative: preliminary inquiry (48hrs, limited data)
- Action: Decide by April 4 whether Panama thread is critical enough for surcharge
- Risk: If we need full beneficial ownership data, preliminary inquiry won't suffice

5. ECI PREMIUM UPGRADE OFFER (LOW PRIORITY - PROMOTIONAL)
- Flash sale expires April 5
- €299 for faster turnaround + Malta/Cyprus deep-dive
- Assessment: We already have Source A for Cyprus; 127 queries remaining in standard package
- Action: DEFER - promotional noise, not critical path blocker
- Decision: Decline upgrade, maximize existing package value

PRIORITIZED ACTION SEQUENCE:
1. [IMMEDIATE] Confirm Source A interview April 7
2. [IMMEDIATE] Assess Singapore documentation gaps, create assembly plan
3. [APRIL 4 AM] Decide Panama registry approach (full vs preliminary)
4. [APRIL 4 PM] Partner coordination call with realistic timeline
5. [APRIL 5] Decline ECI upgrade offer

BLOCKERS TO WATCH:
- If Singapore docs delayed beyond April 6, legal review deadline at risk
- If Source A interview can't happen April 7-9, Cyprus thread weakened significantly
- If Panama requires full access, April 14-17 delivery may conflict with April 18 publication target

response_body.content:
DECISION CONTEXT (April 2, 2026 - 48hr window)

TRIGGER EVENT: GRD promotional email received 09:15 UTC
- Panama premium queries: €18/query (normally €25) 
- 24-hour turnaround guarantee
- 87% beneficial ownership success rate (vs ECI's 73%)
- Offer expires: April 4, 09:00 UTC
- "Limited journalist slots" urgency language

CURRENT STATE - ECI PACKAGE:
✓ Purchased: March 15, €450 total
✓ Consumed: 127 queries (€285 value used)
✗ Remaining: 73 queries (€285 unrecovered value)
✓ Expiration: April 30, 2026
✓ Coverage: Cyprus/Malta/Jersey
✗ Success rate: 73% (below 85% dual-source waiver threshold)
✗ Turnaround: 5-7 days standard processing

REMAINING CLEARVIEW ENTITIES: 27 total
Jurisdiction breakdown from investigation notes:
- Panama: 14 entities (critical path - shell network core)
- Cayman: 8 entities (critical path - beneficial ownership chain)
- Cyprus: 3 entities (non-critical - secondary verification)
- Jersey: 2 entities (non-critical - historical context)

LEGAL CONSTRAINT UPDATE (Rajesh Mehta, April 1):
✓ Dual-source waiver approved IF primary source ≥85% success rate
✓ GRD's 87% rate qualifies for waiver
✗ ECI's 73% rate requires dual-source verification
→ Legal review timeline impact: 4-6 days saved with waiver-qualified vendor

TIMELINE PRESSURE (Sarah Winters/Reuters, March 31):
✗ Publication deadline: April 10 (hard constraint - competitive pressure)
✗ Legal review deadline: April 7 (allows final edits)
✗ Documentation deadline: April 5 (legal review input)
→ Current date: April 2
→ Available buffer: 3 days for 27 entity queries + legal review

DECISION SCENARIOS:

SCENARIO A: Full GRD Switch (abandon ECI)
Cost calculation:
- GRD flash sale: 22 entities × €18 = €396
- ECI sunk cost loss: €285 (73 unused queries)
- Net cost: €681 total
- Additional spend: €396

Timeline impact:
- 24-hour GRD turnaround → documentation ready April 3
- Legal review April 3-6 (3 days, within buffer)
- Meets April 7 deadline with 1-day margin

Quality impact:
- 87% success rate → dual-source waiver approved
- Eliminates 4-6 day secondary verification step
- Certified translations included (saves legal review time)

Risks:
- €285 sunk cost unrecovered (budget efficiency hit)
- Vendor relationship damage with ECI (mid-contract abandonment)
- GRD urgency language may be manipulative (need verification)

SCENARIO B: Hybrid Approach
Cost calculation:
- Use ECI for 5 non-critical entities (Cyprus/Jersey): €0 additional
- GRD for 22 critical entities (Panama/Cayman): 22 × €18 = €396
- ECI sunk cost recovery: ~€15 (5 queries used from remaining 73)
- Net cost: €846 total
- Additional spend: €396

Timeline impact:
- ECI queries: 5-7 days → documentation ready April 7-9
- GRD queries: 24 hours → documentation ready April 3
- Legal review split: critical path April 3-6, non-critical April 7-9
- Meets April 7 deadline for critical entities only
- Non-critical entities miss publication window

Quality impact:
- Critical entities: 87% success rate, dual-source waiver
- Non-critical entities: 73% success rate, requires dual-source
- Mixed legal review complexity

Risks:
- Partial sunk cost recovery (€270 still unrecovered)
- Non-critical entities may miss publication deadline
- Increased coordination complexity (two vendors)

SCENARIO C: ECI-Only Continuation
Cost calculation:
- Use remaining 73 ECI queries: €0 additional
- Net cost: €450 total (already paid)
- Additional spend: €0
- Maximum sunk cost recovery

Timeline impact:
- 5-7 day turnaround → documentation ready April 7-9
- Legal review April 7-13 (includes dual-source verification)
- MISSES April 7 deadline by 6 days
- Publication deadline April 10 not feasible

Quality impact:
- 73% success rate → requires dual-source verification
- Adds 4-6 days to legal review timeline
- Higher defamation risk (below 85% threshold)

Risks:
- Publication deadline failure (competitive disadvantage)
- Partner newsroom coordination breakdown
- Legal review quality concerns (73% success rate)

VENDOR CREDIBILITY CHECK (GRD):
Need to verify:
□ Gmail history: prior GRD promotional emails (pattern analysis)
□ Finance records: past GRD transactions (relationship history)
□ "Limited journalist slots" claim: genuine capacity constraint or artificial urgency?
□ 87% success rate: independently verified or vendor claim?
□ References: Reuters/ICIJ/Guardian mentioned in email - verify?

DECISION CRITERIA WEIGHTING:
1. Timeline compliance (April 10 deadline): CRITICAL
2. Legal review quality (85%+ threshold): HIGH
3. Budget efficiency (sunk cost recovery): MEDIUM
4. Vendor relationship integrity: LOW

NEXT ACTIONS:
□ Search gmail for prior GRD emails (urgency pattern verification)
□ Check finance records for GRD transaction history
□ Cross-reference entity jurisdiction breakdown with investigation notes
□ Calculate legal review timeline buffer under each scenario
□ Draft decision memo documenting tradeoff analysis
□ If choosing A/B: prepare GRD order email with entity list
□ If choosing C: document rationale for future procurement protocol
